text:
Something has to give in Montreal. The Canadiens have points in ten straight (8-0-2) and the Wild in eight straight (6-0-2), and both have the goalie to thank. Jesper Wallstedt leads with 13.3 goals saved above expected this season (goals he has prevented beyond what the shots warranted). Jacob Fowler is right behind at 11.2, and is .935 over his last five starts. That's a lot of saves meeting a lot of saves.

Fowler's week has had a strange subplot. A fan threw an apple at him in Toronto on Saturday, and he has since explained what he told the referee, per the headlines. Meanwhile, as Carey Price enters the Hall of Fame, the comparisons between the two keep arriving.

The difference between these streaks is in the chances. Minnesota has had 57% of the expected goals during its run; Montreal has had 50%, and has been living on Fowler and finishing. The Canadiens are also short two important pieces, Ivan Demidov and Mike Matheson, with Kaiden Guhle up to nearly 25 minutes a night in Matheson's absence. Montreal takes 5.2 penalties a game, the habit we'd worry about most against a Wild power play that creates 0.95 expected goals a game. Our numbers lean Minnesota, 3.32 to 2.90.

Kirill Kaprizov has an eight-game point streak (five goals, nine assists), and we have him at 48% to score. Joel Eriksson Ek is on an eight-game run too. For Montreal, Cole Caufield is 37% to score, Juraj Slafkovský plays his 300th game, and Nick Suzuki is at 70% for a point. Our sleeper is Bobby Brink, a third-liner with dangerous shots against a defense that allows the sixth-most expected goals per 60.
headline: Two point streaks, two hot goalies, one gets snapped

hunch.text: Our numbers expect a bit over six goals. Our gut says both goalies are in that zone where nothing gets by, and this ends 3-2 or tighter.
